name: Purple Pizzazz
lede: Purple Pizzazz is a vivid purple whose naming history is undocumented in the sources ColorHub holds.

sections.title: A playful name, undocumented
sections.body:
Nothing in the sources we hold says who named Purple Pizzazz or when [1]. Our classifier marks it "undocumented," meaning it could not be placed in a word class such as nature, place or pigment the way most of its library neighbors can [1]. The one thing Wikipedia's color list gives us is the hex value and a family label, *Purples* [1].

At lightness 63 and chroma 87, it is one of the most saturated names in that family, brighter than either [[zinzolin]] or plain [[purple]] [1]. Its nearest library neighbor is Orchid, about 6 units away by CIEDE2000, close enough that most eyes would call them the same at a glance [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 museum paintings, as photographed, holds no painting where a patch this bright and this purple-pink covers five percent or more of the canvas [2]. A color this saturated is rare in paint and more common in plastics, dye and screens, which is consistent with a name built for a modern color list rather than a historical pigment [2].
